controls.name: No high-risk Microsoft Defender exclusions
controls.expected: No exclusions for drive roots, temp or download folders, script hosts or executable file types
controls.rationale: Broad exclusions create blind spots. Attackers add Defender exclusions to hide payloads, and overly wide developer exclusions have the same effect.
controls.remediationGuidance: Review each exclusion and remove it with Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath/-ExclusionProcess/-ExclusionExtension. Exclusions are never removed automatically because they are often needed by build tools.

controls.name: Microsoft Defender network protection is in block mode
controls.rationale: Network protection blocks outbound connections to low-reputation and known-malicious domains from any process, not only the browser.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-MpPreference -EnableNetworkProtection Enabled

controls.name: LLMNR multicast name resolution is disabled
controls.message: LLMNR is active and can be poisoned on the local network.
controls.rationale: LLMNR answers can be spoofed by anyone on the local network to capture NTLM credentials (Responder-style poisoning).
controls.remediationGuidance: Set HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient EnableMulticast (DWORD) to 0

controls.name: PowerShell script block logging is on
controls.message: Script block logging is not enabled by policy.
controls.rationale: Script block logging records deobfuscated PowerShell code in event 4104, which is the main evidence source for PowerShell-based attacks. Logged code can include secrets typed into scripts, so restrict access to the PowerShell Operational log.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging EnableScriptBlockLogging (DWORD) to 1

controls.name: Attack surface reduction rules are configured
controls.expected: At least one ASR rule in Block or Warn mode
controls.message: No attack surface reduction rules are configured.
controls.rationale: ASR rules block common malware behaviors such as Office spawning child processes or credential theft from LSASS.
controls.remediationGuidance: Deploy rules in Audit mode first and review events before switching to Block, because ASR rules can interfere with developer tools. See the ASR rules reference.

controls.name: SMB server requires signing
controls.message: SMB signing is negotiated but not required.
controls.rationale: Required SMB signing prevents NTLM relay attacks against this host's file shares.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true -Force. Test first: very old SMB clients and some NAS devices cannot sign.

controls.name: LSA protection (RunAsPPL) is on
controls.message: LSASS does not run as a protected process.
controls.rationale: Running LSASS as a protected process blocks most user-mode credential dumping from LSASS memory.
controls.remediationGuidance: Follow Microsoft's LSA protection guidance: audit incompatible drivers and plug-ins first, then enable and restart.

controls.name: Potentially unwanted application (PUA) blocking is on
controls.message: PUA detections are logged but not blocked.
controls.rationale: PUA protection blocks adware, bundlers and similar software that is not classified as malware.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-MpPreference -PUAProtection Enabled

controls.name: Controlled folder access is on
controls.rationale: Controlled folder access stops untrusted applications from modifying files in protected folders, which limits ransomware damage.
controls.remediationGuidance: Enable in Windows Security > Ransomware protection after allow-listing the development tools you use; it frequently blocks compilers and package managers.

controls.name: PowerShell module logging is on
controls.message: Module logging is not enabled by policy.
controls.rationale: Module logging records pipeline execution details (event 4103). It is noisy, so it is reported as a recommendation rather than a failure.
controls.remediationGuidance: Enable 'Turn on Module Logging' in Group Policy and choose module names deliberately to control log volume.

controls.name: PowerShell transcription is on
controls.message: Transcription is not enabled by policy.
controls.rationale: Transcripts capture full session input and output, including any secrets displayed. Enable only with a protected output directory. Reported for visibility only.
controls.remediationGuidance: Enable 'Turn on PowerShell Transcription' with an OutputDirectory that users cannot read or modify.

controls.name: Microsoft Defender real-time protection is on
controls.rationale: Real-time protection scans files and processes as they are accessed. Without it, Defender only detects malware during scheduled or manual scans.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false

controls.name: Windows Firewall Domain profile is on and blocks unsolicited inbound traffic
controls.rationale: The host firewall is the last network control on a device that roams between networks.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Domain -Enabled True -DefaultInboundAction Block

controls.name: Windows Firewall Private profile is on and blocks unsolicited inbound traffic
controls.rationale: The host firewall is the last network control on a device that roams between networks.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Private -Enabled True -DefaultInboundAction Block

controls.name: Windows Firewall Public profile is on and blocks unsolicited inbound traffic
controls.rationale: The Public profile applies on untrusted networks such as hotel and airport Wi-Fi.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Public -Enabled True -DefaultInboundAction Block

controls.name: Remote Desktop is off or requires Network Level Authentication
controls.expected: fDenyTSConnections = 1, or UserAuthentication = 1 when RDP is enabled
controls.rationale: Network Level Authentication requires credentials before a session is created, which reduces exposure to pre-authentication RDP vulnerabilities.
controls.remediationGuidance: Turn off Remote Desktop if unused, or enable 'Require devices to use Network Level Authentication' in Settings > System > Remote Desktop.

controls.name: SMBv1 server protocol is disabled
controls.rationale: SMBv1 lacks modern integrity protections and was the transport for EternalBlue (MS17-010) exploitation.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false -Force

controls.name: SMBv1 optional feature is removed
controls.expected: SMB1Protocol feature Disabled or not present
controls.rationale: Removing the feature removes both the SMBv1 client and server components, not only the server setting.
controls.remediationGuidance: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol -NoRestart, then restart. Not automated because it needs a restart before it can be verified.

controls.name: User Account Control is on
controls.rationale: With UAC off, every administrator process runs with a full token and malware inherits it without a prompt.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set EnableLUA to 1 under HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System and restart.

controls.name: Built-in Guest account is disabled
controls.rationale: The Guest account allows unauthenticated-style local access and is a well-known default account.
controls.remediationGuidance: Disable-LocalUser -SID <machine SID>-501

controls.name: Microsoft Defender behavior monitoring is on
controls.rationale: Behavior monitoring detects suspicious process activity that signature scanning alone misses.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-MpPreference -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $false

controls.name: Microsoft Defender cloud-delivered protection is on
controls.rationale: Cloud-delivered protection lets Defender query Microsoft's cloud service to block new threats before signatures are published.
controls.remediationGuidance: Set-MpPreference -MAPSReporting Advanced

controls.name: Microsoft Defender antivirus signatures are current
controls.expected: Signatures updated within 3 days (WARN up to 7 days)
controls.rationale: Stale signatures miss recent malware families. The 3 and 7 day thresholds are project defaults, not a vendor requirement.
controls.remediationGuidance: Update-MpSignature

controls.name: Microsoft Defender tamper protection is on
controls.rationale: Tamper protection stops local processes, including malware running as administrator, from turning off Defender features.
controls.remediationGuidance: Turn on Tamper Protection in Windows Security > Virus & threat protection settings, or through Intune. It cannot be changed with PowerShell by design.

controls.name: Windows PowerShell 2.0 engine is removed
controls.expected: MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root feature Disabled or not present
controls.rationale: The 2.0 engine predates script block logging and AMSI, so launching it (powershell -Version 2) bypasses both.
controls.remediationGuidance: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root -NoRestart. Not automated because feature changes need a restart before verification.

controls.name: Secure Boot is on
controls.rationale: Secure Boot only allows signed boot components to load, which blocks boot-level rootkits.
controls.remediationGuidance: Enable Secure Boot in the UEFI firmware settings.

controls.name: BitLocker protects the operating system drive
controls.message: BitLocker cmdlets are not available (for example on Windows Home). Check Device Encryption in Settings.
controls.rationale: Without disk encryption, anyone with physical access to a lost or stolen device can read its data.
controls.remediationGuidance: Enable BitLocker from Control Panel or manage-bde after saving the recovery key somewhere safe. Never enabled automatically: a lost recovery key means lost data.

disclaimer: Framework references show related guidance only. This report is a point-in-time configuration assessment, not a compliance certification.
